paper.title: Temperature Variation-Triggered TRPA1 Activation Induces Intranuclear IL-33 Expression in Trigeminal Ganglion Neurons to Provoke Nasal Hypersensitivity in Idiopathic Rhinitis.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic rhinitis (IR) is characterized by nasal hyperreactivity (NHR), which is frequently triggered by temperature variation (TV), as often observed in clinical practice in autumn and winter. While it is generally believed to be associated with TRP channels and neuroimmune pathways, the specific neuroimmune mechanisms underlying TV-induced IR (TV-IR) remain elusive.

OBJECTIVE: To elucidate the sensory neuroimmune mechanisms underlying TV-IR.

METHODS: Neuropeptide levels in the nasal mucosa from IR patients and controls were assessed by ELISA. A newly established murine model of TV-IR was created using repeated cold exposure. Wild-type, Trpa1-/-, and Il33-/- mice were subjected to the TV-IR model. TV-IR mice were treated with the TRPA1 inhibitor, the substance P receptor antagonist, and the mast cell stabilizer. Inflammatory cytokines and neuropeptides in the trigeminal ganglion were analyzed by immunofluorescence and western blot. ATAC-seq analysis and in vitro loss-of-function and gain-of-function assays were performed on ND7/23 sensory neuron-like cells.

RESULTS: IR patients exhibited increased substance P (SP) levels in nasal mucosa during winter. TV induced IR in mice, with increased expression of SP and neuromedin B (NMB) in nasal mucosa and trigeminal ganglia. The symptoms of NHR and upregulation of SP and NMB in TV-IR were reduced in Trpa1-/- mice, Il33-/- mice, and mice treated with HC030031, QWF, and ketotifen. TV induced excessive neuronal activation and increased the intranuclear expression of IL-33 in neurons of trigeminal ganglia through the Ca2+-calcineurin-NFAT pathway. Il33 deficiency ablated TV-induced neuropeptide expression in trigeminal ganglia neurons. Mechanistically, nuclear IL-33 increased SP and NMB expression by increasing the chromatin accessibility of Tac1 and Nmb.

CONCLUSION: TV activates TRPA1-Ca2+ signaling in sensory neurons to induce their intranuclear level of IL-33, which acts as a nuclear transcription factor to promote neuropeptide synthesis, thereby enhancing mast cell activity. This process serves as a critical mechanism in TV-induced IR and targeting the TRPA1-IL-33-SP-mast cell activation axis represents a potential therapeutic strategy for IR.

paper.title: Functional characterization of olfactory receptor 52E8 and identification of candidate ligands in Japanese eel (Anguilla japonica) larvae.
paper.abstract: Olfactory receptors are G protein-coupled membrane proteins that mediate the detection of environment chemical cues and contribute to foraging and feeding behavior in fish. Japanese eel (Anguilla japonica) is an economically important aquaculture species in East Asia, but the development of effective diets for its larval stages remains a major bottleneck in closed cycle aquaculture. In this study, OR52E8, an olfactory receptor expressed during both the preleptocephalus and leptocephalus stages, was selected for structural and functional characterization. OR52E8 exhibited the conserved seven transmembrane α helices of olfactory receptors and was localized to the olfactory epithelium of female Japanese eels by in situ hybridization. Molecular docking of OR52E8 with 46 candidate feeding attractants identified several potential ligands. A heterologous cell based functional assay further showed that cholic acid (CA) and guanosine 5'-monophosphate (GMP) activated OR52E8 mediated cAMP signaling in a concentration dependent manner. Interaction analysis identified H105 and N180 as potential residues involved in GMP recognition. Alanine substitution of these residues significantly altered GMP induced OR52E8 activation. In summary, CA and GMP were identified as candidate ligands for OR52E8, suggesting that OR52E8 may contribute to the detection of food related chemical cues during the larval stage of Japanese eel. This study provides a molecular basis for further screening of potential feeding stimulants and their functional validation in Japanese eel larvae.

paper.title: Cross-Sensory Taste Modulation and Cultivar-Specific Carotenoid Metabolism: Complementary Perspectives on Tea Flavor Formation.
paper.abstract: Carotenoids are terpenoid metabolites in tea plants (Camellia sinensis) that serve simultaneously as photosynthetic pigments, aroma precursors, and cross-sensory taste regulators. Despite the considerable value of research on tea flavor, existing work is generally categorized into three independent lines of inquiry: cultivar-associated metabolic traits, processing-induced metabolite transformations, and sensory evaluation. This compartmentalization may limit holistic insight into the synergistic regulatory mechanisms among tea flavor profiles. This review integrates the cultivar-specific metabolic basis of tea carotenoids, their degradation and transformation during processing and storage, and the cross-sensory taste modulation mechanisms of carotenoid-derived aroma compounds, and develops a unified framework linking metabolic precursors to sensory perception. Carotenoid biosynthesis is coordinately regulated by genetic background and environmental factors, and germplasm-specific profiles determine flavor potential. During processing and storage, enzymatic and nonenzymatic reactions-including thermal cleavage, photooxidation, and chemical oxidation-convert carotenoids with no direct sensory contribution into characteristic aroma compounds such as β-ionone, β-damascenone, and theaspirone. Different tea processing technologies can therefore be viewed as differentiated chemical programming of a common precursor pool. Carotenoid-derived aromas interact with the sweet taste receptor T1R2/T1R3 via retronasal olfaction and undergo central multisensory integration, enhancing sweetness and suppressing bitterness and astringency. A four-level framework is proposed: genetic metabolic basis, processing material transformation, cross-sensory perceptual integration, and cognitive-emotional evaluation, together with cultivar-process matching strategies. This framework indicates that tea flavor is not a simple sum of volatile and nonvolatile compounds but an emergent outcome of metabolic, chemical, and neural interactions, which can support cultivar selection, processing optimization, and precise quality regulation in tea flavor science.

paper.title: The Increase of Tuft Cells is the Pathological Feature of Nasal Mucosa Type 2 Inflammation, and Indicates the Poor Prognosis of CRSwNP.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is a common chronic airway disease, and eosinophilic CRSwNP (eCRSwNP) is associated with poor prognosis. Tuft cells are associated with type 2 inflammation, but their role in CRSwNP remains unclear.

METHODS: Public single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from nasal mucosal tissues of 21 participants (5 healthy controls, 5 patients with CRSsNP, 5 patients with non-eosinophilic CRSwNP, and 6 patients with eosinophilic CRSwNP) were evaluated, and bulk RNA sequencing, immunofluorescence, and protein correlation analyses were employed to investigate the association between tuft cells and the nasal mucosal type 2 inflammatory microenvironment. A total of 111 participants undergoing nasal surgery were recruited, and 69 CRSwNP patients with over 1-year follow-up were included in the prognostic analysis. CellChat and CellPhoneDB were utilized to explore the communication patterns between tuft cells and type 2 inflammation-related immune cells. Three-fold cross-validated LASSO-Cox regression was used to screen predictors for constructing a prognostic model.

RESULTS: Tuft cells were increased in eCRSwNP and closely associated with type 2 inflammation severity. Moreover, tuft cells were predicted to interact with type 2 inflammation-related immune cells through arachidonic acid metabolites, acetylcholine, and galectin-9. Tuft cell signature genes were closely related to prognosis of patients with CRSwNP. A prognostic model combined with TRPM5 and tissue eosinophil (EOS) counts exhibited high predictive efficacy (AUC = 0.956 in training set, 0.904 in validation set).

CONCLUSION: Tuft cells are increased in eCRSwNP and are associated with the severity of nasal mucosal type 2 inflammation. The tuft cell signature genes, especially TRPM5 combined with tissue EOS counts, can effectively predict the disease control status of CRSwNP patients after functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS). TRPM5 may serve as a potential therapeutic target for eCRSwNP, providing a perspective for precise diagnosis and treatment.

paper.title: Formation and molecular taste perception mechanism of novel L-theanine Amadori products formed during tea drying.
paper.abstract: Amadori rearrangement products (ARPs) are key Maillard reaction intermediates influencing tea flavor, yet systematic studies on L-theanine-derived ARPs (Thea-ARPs) are limited. This work investigates the formation, identification, and taste perception mechanisms of Thea-ARPs formed during tea drying. Results showed temperature-dependent depletion of L-theanine and four monosaccharides, confirming their precursor roles. Four novel Thea-ARPs (N-deoxy-1-L-theanine-D-glucose, N-deoxy-1-L-theanine-L-arabinose, N-deoxy-1-L-theanine-L-rhamnose, and N-deoxy-1-L-theanine-D-galacturonic acid) were structurally characterized. Density functional theory calculations revealed formation energetics with reactivity order: uronic acid (UA) > pentose > hexose. Thea-ARPs were naturally present in various teas, with abundance reflecting both precursor availability and processing conditions. Sensory evaluation identified umami as the dominant taste attribute of Thea-ARPs (thresholds: 0.125-0.5 mg·mL⁻¹). Molecular docking and cellular calcium signaling assays demonstrated that Thea-ARPs activate the umami receptor T1R1/T1R3 through hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions. This work establishes Thea-ARPs as potentially important umami contributors, providing a molecular basis for understanding and regulating tea taste.

paper.title: A study on olfactory mucosa-derived stem cells for ischemic stroke is registered in Hainan.
paper.abstract: On November 4, 2026, China announced that a study on autologous olfactory mucosa-derived mesenchymal stem cells for ischemic stroke was registered in Hainan. Initiated by Hainan Susheng Biotechnology Co., Ltd., the project lists Haikou People's Hospital as its clinical research institution. Olfactory mucosa-derived cells provide a distinct source for investigating immunomodulation and neural repair. A 2025 study of hypoxia-preconditioned cells reported reduced microglial ferroptosis and neuroinflammation and improved neurological outcomes in experimental stroke models. These findings provide a preclinical rationale; the registered product's preparation and its effects in humans need to be clinically evaluated. For Hainan, the project links local scientific work with collaboration between a biotechnology enterprise and a hospital. Its contribution will depend on appropriate patient selection, credible study design, meaningful functional outcomes, reproducible cell manufacture, and long-term safety monitoring. Transparent reporting can make this experience informative for future stroke research and the development of regulated regenerative medicine.

paper.title: Spatial coupling between anosmia-related cortical alterations and regional gene expression: An imaging transcriptomics study.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of anosmia on brain cortical structure and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated causal associations between anosmia and cortical alterations using a multi-modal approach combining neuroimaging and genetics.

METHODS: High-resolution structural magnetic resonance imaging was acquired from 52 patients with anosmia and 50 healthy controls to extract cortical surface area (SA) and cortical thickness (TH). Mendelian randomization (MR) was employed to assess the causal effect of anosmia on cortical structure using summary statistics from the ENIGMA consortium. Furthermore, integrating gene expression data from the Allen Human Brain Atlas (AHBA), partial least squares regression (PLSR) and summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) were used to identify genes associated with changes in SA and TH due to anosmia. Gene enrichment analysis and cell type-specific analysis were then performed to explore the potential molecular mechanisms.

RESULTS: Patients exhibited significantly reduced SA in the left rostral anterior cingulate and superior temporal sulcus, while TH was increased in regions including the left cuneus and supramarginal gyrus. MR analysis identified 11 cortical structural features nominally associated with anosmia, although none survived multiple comparison correction across 138 tests. Transcriptomic analysis identified genes correlated with these structural alterations, which were significantly enriched in synaptic pathways (e.g., postsynaptic membrane modulation) and specifically implicated GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons.

CONCLUSION: Anosmia is causally associated with distinct cortical structural alterations. These regional changes are spatially coupled with molecular signatures involving synaptic function and neuronal plasticity, providing novel insights into the potential pathophysiology of olfactory loss.

paper.title: Orosensory fat taste sensitivity and dietary patterns in young Lebanese adults: a cross-sectional study.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Orosensory fat taste perception (oleogustus) contributes to the detection of dietary fatty acids and may influence eating behavior. This study examined oral fat-taste sensitivity, food preference, and habitual dietary intake in young Lebanese adults.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 117 Lebanese adults aged 18-40 years were recruited between June 2024 and December 2025. Oral sensitivity to linoleic acid was assessed with a sip-and-spit three-alternative forced-choice procedure using 13 concentrations from 0.45 μmol/L to 12 mmol/L; fat-taste detection thresholds were obtained for 108 participants. A receiver-operating-characteristic-derived cut-off of 9 μmol/L defined high (HFS; n = 83) and low (LFS; n = 25) fat-taste sensitivity. Food preference was assessed with a 20-item questionnaire and habitual intake with a 97-item food-frequency questionnaire grouped into 19 predefined categories. Dietary patterns were derived by principal component analysis (PCA) with Varimax rotation, and Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction was applied within each comparison family.

RESULTS: Among 86 participants with complete paired data, 8 of 21 prespecified preference-consumption correlations remained significant after FDR correction (Spearman ρ = 0.282-0.463; all q ≤ 0.025), the strongest being knefeh with Lebanese-dessert consumption (ρ = 0.463, q < 0.001). Nine of the 97 individual food items differed between groups before correction, but none afterwards (smallest q = 0.097). PCA of the 19 categories (n = 86) yielded five patterns explaining 50.35% of the variance; none differed between groups (n = 86) or was associated with LFS after adjustment for age and sex. A post hoc PCA of 16 preselected items (n = 86) yielded three patterns explaining 40.60% of the variance, of which a vegetable and olive pattern scored higher in HFS participants (p = 0.001, q = 0.003) and was associated with lower odds of LFS (OR = 0.28, 95% CI 0.10-0.76; q = 0.036).

CONCLUSION: Reported preference corresponded to habitual consumption for 8 of 21 food pairs, indicating a food-specific rather than uniform relationship between liking and intake. Fat-taste sensitivity was not associated with individual food consumption or with patterns derived from predefined categories. An exploratory analysis of preselected foods identified a vegetable and olive pattern linked to higher sensitivity, a direction that larger and longitudinal studies are well placed to confirm. Combining fat-taste testing with dietary-pattern analysis may help identify individuals at risk of energy-dense diets.

paper.title: TRPM8 channel blockers as a potential new pharmacological class for the treatment of migraine.
paper.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Migraine therapy has advanced in recent years, particularly with the emergence of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)-targeting drugs. However, acute treatment still faces limitations, especially in patients who are unresponsive to or unable to take triptans or gepants. Transient receptor potential melastatin 8 (TRPM8) is a polymodal-gated, nonselective cation channel that represents a promising target for the treatment of migraine, supported by genetic, preclinical, and clinical evidence.

AREAS COVERED: This review covers the evidence supporting an important role for TRPM8 in the pathophysiology of migraine and provides a detailed synopsis of the preclinical, pharmacodynamic, and pharmacokinetic profiles of potential TRPM8-interacting compounds in clinical development for the treatment of migraine. PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through August 2026 for TRPM8 and migraine, supplemented by 2026 congress abstracts and company disclosures.

EXPERT OPINION: TRPM8 channel blockade has a mechanistically distinct approach from current therapeutics. A proof-of-concept and dose‑range‑finding Phase 2 study with elismetrep, a novel, oral TRPM8 blocker, provides supportive, although not definitive, evidence for TRPM8 blockers in migraine. Although the primary endpoint of 2-hour pain freedom was not statistically significant, numerically greater effects at 20 mg and nominally significant secondary-endpoint findings support further development.

paper.title: Nonlinear association between cumulative mean dose to the taste-bud-bearing tongue mucosa and patient-reported taste dysfunction during head and neck IMRT.
paper.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The during-treatment relationship between cumulative mean taste bud dose and taste dysfunction remains incompletely characterized. This retrospective pilot study examined site-related dose variation and nonlinearity of this relationship during head and neck intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT).

METHODS: Thirty-two patients with oropharyngeal (n = 13) or hypopharyngeal/laryngeal (n = 19) cancer received definitive IMRT (70 Gy in 35 fractions). Routine treatment diaries assessed three taste qualities at 10-Gy prescribed-dose milestones (total score, 0-6). Cumulative mean taste bud dose was calculated at each assessment using planning computed tomography contours of the tongue mucosa. Linear mixed-effects models adjusted for age and concurrent chemotherapy compared linear, quadratic, and piecewise forms. An exploratory analysis compared taste bud and extended oral cavity doses.

RESULTS: Despite a uniform prescribed-dose schedule, final mean taste bud dose differed by primary site (median, 42.2 Gy for oropharyngeal vs. 21.2 Gy for hypopharyngeal/laryngeal cancer). The 20-Gy piecewise model improved fit compared with quadratic and linear models. The score increased steeply below 20 Gy (1.99 points per 10 Gy; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.58-2.41) and less steeply above 20 Gy (0.95 points per 10 Gy, 95% CI, 0.42-1.48; both p < 0.001), with a significant change in slope (p < 0.001). Models using oral cavity dose showed similar fit and prediction errors, without a clear advantage for taste bud dose.

CONCLUSION: Cumulative mean taste bud dose showed a nonlinear association with patient-reported taste dysfunction during treatment. These findings support prospective validation of taste-focused dose assessment and planning strategies, without interpreting 20 Gy as a definitive threshold.

paper.title: Allosteric Gating Mechanism Regulates Odorant Selectivity and Antagonism in Odorant Receptors.
paper.abstract: Odorant receptors (ORs) belong to class A G protein-coupled receptors that detect diverse small molecules, yet the steps that link odorant association to receptor-mediated selectivity remain incompletely defined. Here we combined 1.26 milliseconds of all-atom odorant association molecular dynamics simulations (including pilot simulations) with Markov state modeling and cell-based cAMP measurements to examine two human ORs that recognize chemically distinct odorants. In the class I receptor OR51E2, propionate associates via two extracellular pathways gated for selectivity by residues in extracellular loops 2 and 3. The longer alkyl chain heptanoate occupies this gate and reduces propionate association and signaling which is consistent with the observed antagonist behavior of heptanoate. Pocket-expanding mutations at F1554.57 and L1584.60 alter the ECL2-ECL3 gate by permitting longer-chain fatty acids to adopt fully inserted poses that support gate closure, while also attenuating propionate responses. In the class II receptor OR1A1, hydrophobic odorants partition into the membrane and reach the orthosteric site mostly through multiple transmembrane paths. A mutational scan of gating residues and analysis of intermediate-state occupancies suggest that an orthosteric substitution at G1083.36 can bias odorant association path choice. Together, these results support a model in which odorant association paths and gate residence, together with allosteric coupling between the orthosteric site and entry gates, contribute to odorant specificity and antagonism in ORs.

paper.title: Alzheimer's disease and olfactory dysfunction: the role of TNF-α and mechanisms involving ferritin and P-tau199 from an exploratory cross-sectional study.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Olfactory dysfunction (OD) is a common and important symptom at the early stage of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Growing evidence has showed that abnormal iron metabolism played important roles on the development and progression of AD. However, the specific roles and potential mechanisms of abnormal iron metabolism in AD with OD (AD-OD) patients are still unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To explore the iron metabolism changes in brain and the potential neuroinflammatory and neuropathological mechanisms of OD in AD patients.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional study of AD-OD and AD with no OD (AD-nOD) patients with measurements of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers, including iron metabolism-related proteins, neuroinflammatory factors and AD biomarkers.

METHODS: AD patients were divided into AD-OD and AD-nOD groups according to the overall olfactory function assessed by Sniffin' Sticks test. The levels of iron metabolism-related proteins, neuroinflammatory factors and AD biomarkers in CSF were measured.

RESULTS: CSF levels of ferritin, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and phosphorylated tau 199 (P-tau199) in AD-OD group were significantly higher than those in AD-nOD group. Overall olfactory function was significantly and negatively correlated with CSF levels of ferritin, TNF-α and P-tau199 in AD patients. CSF levels of ferritin, TNF-α and P-tau199 were significantly and positively correlated with each other in AD-OD group. TNF-α mediated 29.6% of the effect of ferritin on P-tau199 in CSF.

CONCLUSION: AD-OD is correlated with the elevated CSF levels of ferritin, TNF-α and P-tau199. CSF Ferritin, TNF-α and P-tau199 levels are associated with each other and collectively correlated with OD in AD patients. TNF-α partially mediates the effect of ferritin on P-tau199 in CSF.

paper.title: Roles of Endogenous Components in Flavor Perception and Eating Quality of Cooked Rice.
paper.abstract: Rice flavor is an important contributor to eating quality and consumer acceptance. Recent studies have increasingly linked rice flavor with the processes underlying its formation, expression, and perception during cooking and consumption. This review critically synthesizes current knowledge on rice flavor and its contribution to eating quality. The major aroma, taste, and texture characteristics of cooked rice are described, focusing on sensory descriptors, volatile and taste-active compounds, and interactions among volatile compounds. The changes in flavor perception during consumption are discussed in relation to oral processing, including mastication, saliva incorporation, bolus formation, texture changes, and retronasal aroma release. The formation of flavor-related compounds is reviewed with respect to genetic background, environmental conditions, and agronomic practices. The roles of major endogenous components, particularly starch, proteins, and lipids, in flavor expression are also discussed. Their interactions with flavor compounds and effects on the physicochemical properties of rice are further considered. This review contributes to a better understanding of rice flavor and its relationship with eating quality, providing a foundation for the evaluation and regulation of rice quality.

paper.title: Characterization of the structure-activity relationships of sweet peptides and their molecular mechanism for human sweet taste receptor activation.
paper.abstract: As promising sugar substitutes, sweet peptides elicit sweetness perception primarily mediated by the heterodimeric sweet taste receptor composed of T1R2 and T1R3 subunits. Therefore, in-depth investigation into their structure-activity relationships is crucial not only for elucidating their molecular recognition mechanisms but also for guiding the rational design of novel peptide-derived sweeteners to improve human dietary health. Existing studies on sweet peptides are mainly restricted to purification and sensory evaluation, or specific dipeptides such as aspartame and neotame. In this study, we firstly determined the sensory profiles of several sweet peptides. Furthermore, the cellular calcium flux assay was utilized to evaluate their biological activities in vitro, and the spatial topology of the sweet peptides was explained based on the classical AH-B-X sweet taste theory. Moreover, the molecular mechanisms governing their activation of the human T1R2/T1R3 sweet taste receptor were illuminated by molecular simulations. Overall, this work provides meaningful insights into the structure-activity relationships of sweet peptides.

paper.title: First bite syndrome in neurologic practice: A narrative review of a distinct paroxysmal craniofacial pain syndrome.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This narrative review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the etiopathogenesis, clinical features, diagnosis, and treatment of first bite syndrome.

BACKGROUND: Though well described by the Otolaryngology and Maxillofacial surgical specialties, first bite syndrome is rarely discussed in Neurology literature. Headache specialists may see these patients as a referral for trigeminal neuralgia or undiagnosed paroxysmal facial pain.

METHODS: Relevant literature was identified through searches of major medical databases from their inception until May 29, 2026. After removing duplicates and excluded abstracts (e.g., incorrect subject matter, non-English, abstract only) and adding additional articles identified from references of reviewed articles, 163 unique articles on first bite syndrome were further analyzed for information on etiology, clinical presentation, prognosis, or treatment.

RESULTS: First bite syndrome typically presents with unilateral paroxysmal facial pain along the parotid and mandibular region, triggered by salivation. The pain is worsened by strong sialagogues such as acidic or sour foods and tends to improve after the first few bites of a meal. It may be aching/cramping or sharp, shock-like pain along the jaw or mandible, and can be mistaken for trigeminal neuralgia or temporomandibular disease. Individuals with first bite syndrome may experience gradual improvement with time, and a smaller number may experience complete resolution of symptoms. For those who do not improve, or for those with severe pain, neuropathic medications or botulinum toxin administration may be beneficial.

Clinicians should be familiar with its clinical presentation and maintain a high index of suspicion when patients present with facial pain associated with salivation. Differentiation of first bite syndrome from other causes of facial pain is important to guide evaluation and therapy, and to help avoid unnecessary medications and procedures.

paper.title: A Transcriptomic Analysis of Putative Gustatory Receptor Genes in Two Hawkmoth Species (Lapara coniferarum and Sphinx dollii).

paper.title: Olfactory Disorders in Children: A Clinical Approach to Aetiologies, Psychophysical Testing and Therapeutics.
paper.abstract:
AIM: Olfaction is a critical physiological function, yet paediatric olfactory dysfunction remains poorly characterized compared to adult populations. This narrative review aims to synthesize current knowledge regarding the aetiology, diagnosis and management of olfactory disorders in children to provide a practical guide for general paediatricians and otolaryngologists.

METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed/Medline, Scopus and Embase. A total of 425 peer-reviewed clinical trials, observational studies and guidelines focusing on paediatric olfaction were evaluated and 41 highly relevant articles were included.

RESULTS: The exact prevalence of paediatric olfactory disorders remains unclear, though it is highly underdiagnosed. Unlike adult presentations, paediatric aetiologies are predominantly congenital (accounting for roughly two-thirds of cases, such as Kallmann syndrome), while acquired causes (traumatic brain injury, post-viral) account for one-third. Diagnostic modalities must be age-appropriately tailored; tools like the 'U-Sniff' or 'Smell Wheel' are required for younger children, alongside high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to evaluate olfactory bulb aplasia. Therapies range from surgical correction for conductive losses to targeted olfactory training for sensorineural deficits.

CONCLUSION: Olfactory disorders in children carry potential safety and developmental consequences. Implementing age-adapted testing and systematic clinical pathways is essential for improving diagnosis and patient outcomes in paediatric practice.

paper.title: Relationship between salt taste sensitivity threshold (STST) and dietary sodium consumption among multi-ethnic older adults in Malaysia.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Salt taste sensitivity threshold (STST) is linked to sodium consumption, particularly among older adults. Reduced salt taste perception as people age may change how flavours are recognized, leading to compensatory behaviours like consuming more salt or favouring foods high in sodium. Excessive consumption of sodium over time raises blood pressure, increases cardiovascular strain, and may negatively impact cerebrovascular health, all of which increase the risk of cognitive impairment. However, to our knowledge, no studies have specifically examined the relationship between STST and sodium consumption among Malaysian older adults. This study investigated the relationship between STST and sodium consumption using dietary assessment and 24-hour urinary sodium excretion (24HUNaV).

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 180 older adults (≥ 60 years) from Pusat Aktiviti Warga Emas (PAWE) in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor. Sodium consumption was assessed using the Salt Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ-Na) and 24HUNaV. STST was measured by the intraoral dropping method with sodium chloride solutions categorized according to population percentiles as low STST (< 30 mmol/L), moderate STST (30-120 mmol/L) and high STST (> 120 mmol/L). Multinomial logistic regression (MLR) determined associations between STST and sodium consumption.

RESULTS: Older adults in the low STST group had the longest years of formal education (11.5 ± 3.6 years), whereas those in the high STST group showed the highest prevalence of denture use (61.3%). Mean sodium consumption was 1936.9 mg/day (FFQ-Na) and 2839.6 mg/day (24HUNaV). In adjusted models, FFQ-Na consumption was associated with moderate STST (aOR = 1.99, 95% CI: 1.23-3.22) and high STST (aOR = 2.20, 95% CI: 1.35-3.59) while 24HUNaV showed a similar association with moderate STST (aOR = 1.59, 95% CI: 1.07-2.37).

CONCLUSION: Higher sodium consumption was associated with elevated STST among multi-ethnic Malaysian older adults. Those with reduced salt taste sensitivity tend to consume more sodium. STST may have potential utility for identifying older adults who may benefit from further dietary sodium assessment.

paper.title: Odor identification versus verbal and facial semantic memory in Parkinson's disease: diagnostic performance and item-specific analysis.

paper.title: Sour Suppresses Sweet, Salty, and Bitter: Implications for Signal Processing in Taste Buds.

paper.title: Distinct patterns of multisensory integration underly the expression of flavor preferences and aversions in rats.
paper.abstract: Flavor is an inherently multisensory experience, combining gustatory and retronasal odor signals during consumption. Previous work has shown that rats weight taste and odor components of flavor mixture solutions to express flavor preferences. However, a comprehensive quantitative understanding of taste-odor integration is lacking. Here, we evaluated the validity of the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) framework for explaining multisensory integration of taste and odor signals toward hedonic flavor judgments. MLE is a dominant framework for explaining multisensory integration in a wide variety of contexts, and states that components of a mixture are weighted according to their relative reliability, resulting in more reliable multisensory judgments. In our experiment, rats expressed preferences for taste, odor and taste+odor solutions in a series of two-bottle preference tests featuring an unpalatable odor component (amyl acetate), and either a palatable taste component (sucrose) or an unpalatable taste component (citric acid). Taste reliability was experimentally varied by presenting taste components at two different concentrations. Reliability of animals' preference judgements was quantified as the variance in preference across repetitions of the same conditions in the same animals. Our results confirm that preferences for mixtures featuring a palatable taste can be described as a weighted average of the component preferences where the weights depend on the relative reliability of the components-a finding that is in line with the MLE framework. However-contrary to MLE-component weighting does not increase the reliability of multisensory preference judgments themselves. In addition, preferences for taste+odor mixtures featuring an unpalatable taste follow a qualitatively different pattern: taste and odor components are combined to enhance flavor rejection judgements. These results demonstrate that the multisensory integrative principles underlying flavor preference differ from other multisensory domains and depend on the valence of the flavor components.

paper.title: Olfactory Reference Symptoms in Adolescents: Functional Impact, Odor-Related/Hygiene Behaviors, and Associations with Anxiety, Depression, and Prodromal-Like Experiences.
paper.abstract: Background: Olfactory reference symptoms involve persistent concerns about emitting an unpleasant body odor and may be accompanied by social avoidance, repetitive behaviors, and functional difficulties. This study examined symptom severity, self-reported functional impact, odor-related/hygiene behaviors, and associated psychopathological dimensions in adolescents. Methods: This cross-sectional online survey included 105 adolescents. Participants completed the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale Modified for Olfactory Reference Syndrome (ORS-YBOCS), Revised Child Anxiety and Depression Scale (RCADS), Prodromal Questionnaire-Brief (PQ-B), and Somatosensory Amplification Scale (SSAS), together with sociodemographic questions and items assessing functional impact and odor-related/hygiene behaviors. Primary associations were examined using Spearman correlations and hierarchical multiple linear regression controlling for age and sex. Results: The mean ORS-YBOCS total score was 10.68 ± 8.04. Participants most commonly reported body-odor-related difficulties in social activities, school attendance, friendships, and romantic interactions. Common behaviors included excessive washing, odor masking, checking, airing out the environment, and sniffing the perceived odor source. ORS-YBOCS scores were positively correlated with RCADS, SSAS, and PQ-B total scores. Social anxiety/social phobia showed the largest correlation among RCADS subscales. In the final regression model, RCADS and PQ-B total scores remained independently associated with higher ORS-YBOCS scores, whereas SSAS was not independently significant. Conclusion: Olfactory reference symptoms in adolescents were associated with functional impact, odor-related/hygiene behaviors, anxiety-depression symptoms, somatosensory amplification, and prodromal-like experiences. Anxiety-depression symptom burden and prodromal-like experiences remained independently associated with symptom severity, supporting the clinical relevance of body-odor concerns as a multidimensional symptom domain.

paper.title: Intrinsic Sweetness and Sweetness-Enhancing Property of β-Damascone.
paper.abstract: β-Damascone is a naturally occurring aroma compound with pronounced fruity-floral and "sweet-smelling" notes. Although well characterized olfactorily, its gustatory role and sweetness-enhancing property remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the intrinsic sweetness of β-damascone and its ability to enhance sucrose-induced sweetness using an integrative approach combining sensory evaluation, electroencephalography (EEG), molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. Sensory evaluation showed that β-damascone alone elicited negligible sweetness, but significantly amplified and prolonged sucrose-induced sweetness. EEG measurements further revealed strengthened cortical responses during co-stimulation with sucrose. Using a cryo-EM-derived full-length TAS1R2-TAS1R3-membrane model, molecular simulations demonstrated that β-damascone binds to a peripheral region of LB1-LB2 cleft in TAS1R2 VFD, stabilizing its closed conformation. β-Damascone also facilitated conformational rearrangements associated with receptor activation, including widening of the intracellular G-protein-binding cavity. Collectively, these findings provide mechanistic evidence that β-damascone acts as a synergistic enhancer of sucrose sweetness, supporting its potential for sugar-reduction applications.

paper.title: Development of a sustained-release 1-Octen-3-ol nanoparticle formulation via molecular docking-guided design and response surface optimization for enhanced mosquito attraction.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mosquito-borne diseases pose a major global health burden, and effective attractants are essential for vector surveillance and control. 1-Octen-3-ol (octenol) is a known mosquito attractant but suffers from high volatility and short effective duration. In this study, molecular docking confirmed its strong binding to mosquito olfactory receptors, providing theoretical support for its attractant activity. To address this limitation, the aim was to develop a nanoparticle encapsulation strategy for sustained release and enhanced stability.

RESULTS: Molecular docking confirmed strong binding affinity between octenol and mosquito olfactory receptors, supporting its attractant activity. Formulation and process parameters were screened via single-factor experiments and optimized using response surface methodology. Under the optimized conditions, octenol-loaded nanoparticles (octenol NPs) exhibited a mean particle size of 142.5 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.1383, a zeta potential of -16.2 mV, a drug loading of 10.9%, and an encapsulation efficiency of 70.2%. Physicochemical characterization demonstrated the favorable stability of octenol NPs, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed successful drug encapsulation. In outdoor mosquito-attraction assays, octenol NPs were 2.98-fold higher than that of an equivalent amount of free octenol in attracting mosquitoes and significantly prolonged the effective half-life of attraction.

CONCLUSION: Nanoparticle encapsulation overcomes octenol's volatility and short activity duration. The optimized octenol NPs provide an efficient, long-lasting mosquito-attractant formulation for vector control. Furthermore, this work establishes a flexible nanocarrier platform for the sustained release of volatile semiochemicals, bridging attractant research with practical applications in mosquito control, and offering broader potential for agricultural arthropod pest management. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

paper.title: Biological Reconstruction of the Anterior Skull Base Using Liquid Nitrogen-Treated Autologous Bone.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rigid skeletal restoration after anterior skull base resection remains unresolved. Alloplastic implants increase exposure and infection risk, whereas vascularized bone flaps increase donor-site morbidity. Liquid nitrogen (LN2)-treated autologous bone, Tsuchiya method, is unexplored for anterior skull base reconstruction.

METHODS: We report cases of two patients (48-year-old man with olfactory neuroblastoma and 50-year-old woman with SMARCB1-deficient chondromyxoid tumor) undergoing anterior craniofacial resection with rigid reconstruction using LN2-treated autologous bone. After periosteal-plane tumor stripping, the bone underwent one LN2 cycle and was re-implanted; the skull base was sealed with a free flap, and the graft was covered with a vascularized pericranial flap. Margins were negative.

RESULTS: At 34 and 33 months, both patients remained disease-free without graft interface recurrence or graft resorption.

CONCLUSIONS: The technique, with preserved margins, thus appears feasible and oncologically defensible in selected patients. We propose a three-criterion indication framework and call for its prospective validation.

paper.title: Bilateral Sinonasal Glomangiopericytoma Originating From the Posterior Nasal Septum.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sinonasal glomangiopericytoma (GPC) is a rare perivascular tumor of the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses, accounting for <0.5% of sinonasal tumors. It typically presents with nonspecific symptoms such as nasal obstruction and epistaxis, and definitive diagnosis relies on histopathologic and immunohistochemical assessment.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 53-year-old medically free male presented with a 7-month history of progressive left-predominant nasal obstruction, intermittent epistaxis, blood-stained purulent nasal discharge, and hyposmia. Endoscopic examination revealed a friable vascular mass arising bilaterally from the olfactory groove/posterior septal region. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated bilateral enhancing soft-tissue lesions centered along the posterior nasal septum, without skull base erosion, orbital involvement, or intracranial extension. Office-based biopsy confirmed sinonasal GPC.

MANAGEMENT AND OUTCOME: The patient underwent complete endoscopic tumor excision under general anesthesia with functional endoscopic sinus surgery, coblation-assisted resection of the septal attachment, bilateral middle turbinate resection, and superior septectomy. Frozen section confirmed GPC. The postoperative course was uneventful, with complete symptom resolution and no endoscopic evidence of residual or recurrent disease at 9-month follow-up.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights an uncommon bilateral presentation of sinonasal GPC arising from the posterior nasal septum. Complete endoscopic excision with careful identification of the tumor attachment can provide excellent clinical outcomes, although long-term endoscopic surveillance remains essential due to the risk of delayed recurrence.

paper.title: The impact of ambient and wildfire-specific air pollution on upper airway disease.
paper.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Ambient air pollution (AAP) and wildfire-specific air pollution (WAP) exposure is increasingly prevalent, yet its effects on upper airway disease remain incompletely characterized. This review updates the evidence linking AAP and WAP to chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS), olfactory dysfunction (OD), allergic rhinitis (AR), and head and neck aerodigestive cancer (HNC).

RECENT FINDINGS: Large biobank- and claims-based studies published in recent years strengthen associations between AAP and both AR and CRS incidence, with newer evidence that pollution may also shape inflammatory endotype and treatment response, including blunted postsurgical symptom improvement after endoscopic sinus surgery. Wildfire-specific data demonstrates dose-dependent association with acute rhinosinusitis healthcare utilization and association with increased head and neck cancer incidence.

SUMMARY: This expanding evidence base positions AAP and WAP as an emerging, modifiable risk factor in upper airway disease, spanning incidence, phenotype, symptom burden, and treatment response. Persistent gaps underscore the need for standardized, prospective, mechanistically grounded studies to guide clinical risk counseling and public health policy as global trends in AAP and wildfire frequency continue to rise.

paper.title: Identification of Type 1 and Type 2 α-Synuclein-Seeds by CSF Seed Amplification Assay in Patients With Movement Disorders.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: A novel α-synuclein (syn) seed amplification assay (synSAA) differentiates 2 types of syn-seeds in CSF: type1, associated with Lewy bodies (LBs), and type2, associated with glial-cytoplasmic inclusions, the hallmark of multiple system atrophy (MSA). However, syn-copathology extends beyond synucleinopathies, and copathologies are increasingly relevant. Different syn-seeds have been assessed in highly characterized research cohorts, but data assessing type and frequency in patients from routine clinical encounters are lacking. Hence, our objective was to determine frequency, type, and clinical association of different syn-seeds in CSF in a large cohort from a movement disorders (MDs) clinic.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included consecutive patients from a MD clinic between 2009 and 2025. CSF was tested with synSAA and clinical data derived from medical records.

RESULTS: We recruited 1,059 patients (mean age 70.5 ± 10.5 years; 38.4% female; mean disease duration 4.0 ± 4.6 years). Syn-seeds were detected in 54.2% of patients, with type1-seeds predominating (88.5%). High synSAA positivity was observed in Parkinson disease (PD) (84.7%), dementia with LB (93.4%), MSA (84.5%), isolated REM-sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) (80.0%), and normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) with PD (87.0%). Undetermined hypokinetic MD showed 53.7% positivity. Moderate proportions (∼25-33%) were detected in Alzheimer disease, progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), corticobasal syndrome, and idiopathic NPH without PD, while other neurologic disorders showed 20.9% positivity. Type2-seeds were the major seed type in MSA (79.6% of syn-seeds) and minor type in PD (6.2%), PSP (9.1%), and undetermined hypokinetic MD (13.8%). Overall, type2-seeds were present in only 2.6% of non-MSA patients. Patients with type1-seeds had worse olfaction and more hallucinations. Multivariable regression identified impaired olfaction (OR = 0.67 per point increase of identified smells out of 12, higher scores indicating better olfaction) significantly associated with type1-seeds.

DISCUSSION: Our results provide reference data on syn-seed frequency in routine clinical patients, demonstrating that type1-seeds indicate common underlying syn-pathology or copathology associated with hyposmia and hallucinations. Type2-seeds are specific to MSA and detection of type2-seeds outside the clinical MSA spectrum can improve diagnosis of patients with atypical presentations because our results match neuropathologic MSA studies. In vivo identification of different seed types will improve diagnosis, clinical trial stratification, and development of targeted therapies.

paper.title: Organization and quantitative analysis of the antennal lobe glomeruli of the yellow peach moth Conogethes punctiferalis.
paper.abstract: The yellow peach moth, Conogethes punctiferali, is a polyphagous pest equipped with two sets of well-developed olfactory organs, antennae and labial palps. With the intention of studying olfactory sensory projections in the antennal lobe, we performed anterograde staining of the sensory neurons on both the antennae and the labial palps. These experiments were combined with synapsin immunohistochemistry for visualizing the neuropil regions in the antennal lobe. The results revealed that each antennal lobe receives ipsilateral projections from the antenna, forming numerous spheroidal glomeruli. The labial palp axons, on the other hand, project both ipsilaterally and contralaterally to one distinct glomerulus, the labial-palp pit organ glomerulus (LPOG), in each antennal lobe. All the glomeruli could be identified based on position, shape, and size. In total, there were 69-71 glomeruli in each antennal lobe of males and females. Apart from LPOG, the glomeruli were classified into sex-specific glomeruli and ordinary glomeruli (OGs). Males possessed three male-specific glomeruli, whereas females had five female-specific glomeruli; both sexes contained 65 OGs. The summed volume of glomeruli in males was about 1437 (×103 μm3), which is smaller than that of females, 1519 (×103 μm3). Nevertheless, the total volume of male-specific glomeruli was 253 (×103 μm3), which is larger than that of female-specific glomeruli, 122 (×103 μm3). The volume of LPOG in females was larger than that of males. A substantial proportion of OGs exhibit sexual isomorphy in size. The volume of most OGs ranged from 10 to 30 (×103 μm3). Altogether, this study characterized the olfactory architecture of the antennal lobe in the yellow peach moth, and revealed its organizational features are consistent with those of other moths, providing a foundation for future research on the neural mechanisms of olfaction of moths.

paper.title: Revealing candidate characteristic markers of wheat aroma: Insights from both saline-alkali stress and mill stream fractions.
paper.abstract: Considering it was widely realized that wheat cultivated in saline-alkali soils and late reduction flour exhibit a stronger wheat aroma than those from normal soils and the early reduction flour, respectively, three wheat varieties cultivated simultaneously in areas with varying salinity and alkalinity levels were used to prepare four mill stream fractions (center to periphery). ROAV analysis further indicated that 5-methylfurfural, γ-butyrolactone (detected via GC-MS), γ-nonalactone, and 3-methylbutanoic acid were generally between 0.1 and 100. These findings provide an integrated screening approach for identifying candidate wheat aroma-associated VOCs under cultivation environments with varying salinity and alkalinity levels and milling fractions.

paper.title: Functional characterization of CpunOR39 reveals oviposition-attractive volatiles in Conogethes punctiferalis (Lepidoptera: Crambidae).
paper.abstract: Olfactory receptors (ORs) play crucial roles in insect chemosensation and influence behaviours such as host selection and oviposition. In this study, we functionally characterized the odorant receptor CpunOR39 in the yellow peach moth, Conogethes punctiferalis, and assessed its relevance to plant-volatile perception. Using two-electrode voltage-clamp (TEVC) recordings coupled with Xenopus laevis oocyte expression, we screened 83 volatile compounds and found that β-ionone, (S)-cis-verbenol and farnesol elicited responses from CpunOR39/CpunOrco-expressing oocytes. β-ionone produced the strongest response (136.99 ± 1.35 nA), followed by (S)-cis-verbenol (102.28 ± 1.25 nA), whereas farnesol elicited a weaker response (45.22 ± 1.36 nA). Dose-response analyses confirmed sensitivity of recombinant CpunOR39 to β-ionone and (S)-cis-verbenol, with EC50 values of 1.0 × 10-5 M and 5.4 × 10-5 M, respectively. RT-qPCR measurement showed that CpunOR39 was enriched in antennae and expressed at higher levels in female antennae than in male antennae. Electroantennography (EAG) assays showed dose-dependent antennal responses of mated and unmated females to the three active compounds, with stronger responses to β-ionone and (S)-cis-verbenol than to farnesol. In behavioural trials, mated females were attracted to β-ionone and (S)-cis-verbenol at higher concentrations and females laid significantly more eggs on substrates treated with β-ionone or (S)-cis-verbenol than on solvent controls, whereas farnesol had no significant effect on oviposition. These findings suggest that CpunOR39 may contribute to the detection of host-associated volatiles involved in oviposition-related behaviours in C. punctiferalis.

paper.title: Prognostic value of OR51T1 expression in men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer.
paper.abstract: Background The olfactory receptor genes (ORs), the largest superfamily in the human genome, are expressed not only in the neurons of the olfactory epithelium but also in various other tissues. We here investigated OR51T1 expression as a potential biomarker for predicting survival among men treated with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC). Methods Sixty-nine men with mHSPC to the bone diagnosed from 2006 to 2015 were enrolled in this retrospective study. All patients had received ADT as first-line treatment. Prostate needle biopsy specimens obtained before the treatment were immunohistochemically stained for OR51T1. Correlations between OR51T1 expression and clinicopathological factors were analyzed using a Cox proportional hazard model. We also examined the expression of OR51T1 in prostate cancer cells and also evaluated the efficacy of suppressing OR51T1 for prostate cancer proliferation. Results Of 69 cases, 43 (62.3%) and 26 (37.7%) showed low and high OR51T1 expression, respectively. Patients with high OR51T1 tumor had a significantly shorter time to castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) development than those with low expression. Multivariate analysis showed that the extent of disease on bone scan (EOD) (3-4 vs. 1-2: HR = 3.1, 95% CI = 1.6-6.2, p=0.001) and OR51T1 expression (high vs. low: HR = 2.3, 95% CI = 1.2-4.4, p=0.014) were independent predictors for CRPC. Patients with high OR51T1 tumor also had a significantly shorter overall survival (OS) than those with low expression. T stage (4 vs ≤3: HR = 3.6, 95% CI = 1.1-11.2, p=0.029), N stage (1 vs 0: HR = 3.0, 95% CI = 1.3-7.1, p=0.010), EOD (3-4 vs. 1-2: HR = 3.7, 95% CI = 1.6-8.5, p=0.003), and OR51T1 expression (high vs. low: HR = 2.2, 95% CI = 1.0-4.8, p=0.038) were independent prognosticators for OS. The OR51T1 expression was high in the prostate cancer cell line PC3. Furthermore, suppressing OR51T1 inhibited cell proliferation in the MTT assay. Conclusions OR51T1 expression is a potential prognostic biomarker for time to CRPC and OS in men undergoing ADT for mHSPC. In OR51T1-expressing prostate cancer cell lines, suppression of OR51T1 inhibited tumor proliferation.

paper.title: Protein language model-assisted screening of bitter peptides from Prunus dulcis.
paper.abstract: Bitterness is a major limitation in the utilization of plant-derived proteins in food systems, while conventional identification of bitter peptides is labor-intensive and inefficient. Advances in food informatics, particularly protein language models, provide new opportunities for predicting the properties of food chemicals. In this study, we developed a protein language model-assisted workflow to screen and prioritize potential bitter peptides from Prunus dulcis proteins. Protein sequences were first subjected to in silico digestion to generate candidate peptides. Representations derived from ESM Cambrian (ESMC) embeddings were combined with amino acid index (AAI) descriptors and Binary Profile-based Numerical Coding (BPNC) features to construct a machine learning model for bitterness prediction. The resulting candidates were further prioritized based on their interaction with the bitter taste receptor TAS2R14 using the ConPLex framework. Three peptides, GECIL, GRPR, and GIPEV, were selected for further evaluation. HPLC analysis revealed hydrolysate peaks with retention times consistent with those of the corresponding synthetic standards, providing preliminary chromatographic evidence, and electronic tongue measurements indicated bitterness-related instrumental responses. CCK-8 assays indicated generally maintained cell viability, except for a decrease with GIPEV at 3.2 mg mL-1. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations suggested stable interaction profiles with TAS2R14, with residues S265 and Q266 likely involved in ligand recognition. This study presents an integrated food informatics workflow combining protein language models with structural and experimental evaluation. The proposed strategy provides a useful approach for discovering bitterness-related peptides from plant proteins and offers insight into the molecular basis of peptide bitterness.

paper.title: The world smells different in Parkinson's disease.
paper.abstract: Olfactory decline is an early sign of Parkinson's disease (PD), often preceding motor symptoms by years to decades. However, because olfactory impairment is also common in healthy and diseased aging, current olfactory performance tests (odor detection, discrimination, and identification) lack disease specificity. In contrast to performance scores, odor-rating-derived olfactory perceptual fingerprints provide a stable measure of how the world smells to an individual. Here, we combine such fingerprints with odor-evoked sniff-response behavior to define an olfactory perceptual-motor signature. To test the hypothesis that this provides a disease-specific marker, we obtained such signatures in three cohorts: Individuals with PD (n = 33), healthy age-matched controls (n = 33), and critically, in participants with non-PD olfactory dysfunction (n = 28). Consistent with previous results, a standard clinical olfactory test detected impairment in both PD and non-PD olfactory dysfunction, but failed to distinguish between these two groups. In contrast, the olfactory perceptual-motor signature both detected impairment and classified PD from non-PD olfactory dysfunction at 94% accuracy (SVM classification, leave-one-out cross-validation, 100% sensitivity, 88% specificity, P = 0.0047). These results dovetail with evidence from vision and audition, implying a perceptual shift rather than only a perceptual decline in PD, and point to the olfactory perceptual-motor signature as a possible disease-specific marker.

paper.title: Fever-induced OR560 promotes antibacterial immunity through macrophage pseudopod formation and phagocytosis.
paper.abstract: Fever is a conserved physiological response to pathogen infection. However, how fever promotes host defense remains poorly understood. Here we find that fever empowers antibacterial immunity by inducing olfactory receptor 560 (OR560) to promote macrophage phagocytosis. paper.title: Feline intestinal organoids reveal cell type-specific tropism and antiviral responses to type II feline infectious peritonitis virus.
paper.abstract: Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV), a highly pathogenic feline coronavirus (FCoV), causes a nearly uniformly fatal disease in cats, yet its infection dynamics within the intestinal epithelium-the primary site of viral entry and replication-remain largely unresolved. Here, we report the first establishment of long-term, passageable three-dimensional (3D) feline intestinal organoids, including feline ileal organoids (fILOs) and feline colonic organoids (fCOs), which faithfully recapitulate the cellular diversity and architecture of the feline intestine and support infection by type II FIPV. Using this physiologically relevant platform, we demonstrate that FIPV infection induces profound epithelial remodeling in fCOs, characterized by a marked expansion of proliferative cell populations and depletion of differentiated epithelial lineages. High-resolution single-cell RNA sequencing of fCOs revealed pronounced cell type-specific viral tropism, with preferential infection of differentiated epithelial cells, particularly goblet and tuft cells, while stem and transit-amplifying cells exhibited relative resistance. This differential susceptibility was strongly associated with cell type-specific expression of host entry and trafficking factors, including aminopeptidase N (APN), TMPRSS2, and Niemann-Pick C1 (NPC1). Importantly, our organoid-based infection model recapitulated in vivo-relevant antiviral responses, enabling robust evaluation of therapeutic candidates and accurately reflecting the potent antiviral efficacy of GS-441524 and the neutralizing antibody 1AF10. Collectively, this study establishes a novel, scalable, and physiologically faithful feline intestinal organoid platform that provides unprecedented insight into type II FIPV epithelial tropism and pathogenesis, and represents a powerful preclinical tool for accelerating the development of effective antiviral and preventive strategies against feline infectious peritonitis.

paper.title: Glioblastoma-Neuroblastoma Cocultured Multicellular Spheroid Model for Evaluating Temozolomide Response.
paper.abstract: Glioblastoma is the most lethal primary brain tumor, and its resistance to therapy is increasingly understood to arise not from tumor cells alone but also from their integration into the surrounding neural circuitry. This indicates that the neuronal-lineage surrogate population alters the overall TMZ response of the coculture spheroids. Drug-response data from glioblastoma only models may therefore not reflect true tumor behavior in the presence of neuronal-lineage cells, supporting the inclusion of neuronal-lineage surrogate components in preclinical glioblastoma drug screening.

paper.title: α-Synuclein Propagation Mouse Models of Parkinson's Disease.

These features of α-Syn PFF-injected animal models provide a platform for exploring disease mechanisms and testing disease-modifying therapies in PD research. paper.title: Recent Progress of Machine Learning Technology in Gas Sensing and Detection.
paper.abstract: Although gas sensing technologies are widely applied in environmental monitoring, industrial safety, and food testing, their applications remain constrained by several challenges, including cross-sensitivity, long-term drift, environmental interference, and slow response. Machine learning (ML) provides new opportunities for intelligent gas sensing by extracting useful patterns from complex sensing signals and improving gas recognition and quantitative analysis. Adopting a problem-oriented perspective, this review examines recent progress of machine learning technology in gas sensing and detection. First, ML methods used in gas sensing are introduced according to learning paradigms and sensing tasks. The applications of these methods in solving key gas-sensing problems are then discussed. Specifically, extracting multichannel and dynamic response features improves gas discrimination; domain adaptation and active learning can compensate for gas drift, whereas including temperature and humidity signals can reduce environmental interference; early-response analysis enables faster gas detection without waiting for steady-state responses. This review further discusses the challenges that limit the practical deployment of ML-based gas sensing systems. Potential solutions, transferable from intelligent sensing applications in other fields, are introduced to solve data scarcity, edge deployment difficulty, and poor interpretability problems, such as data-efficient learning, lightweight model design, and interpretable modeling. Finally, future perspectives such as biomimetic olfactory systems, embodied intelligence for gas source tracking, and AI-assisted analysis of new gas sensing materials are discussed. This review provides an overview of the recent progress of machine learning technology in gas sensing, highlighting future opportunities for developing reliable and automatic gas detection systems.

paper.title: A state-dependent neural circuit resolves approach-avoidance conflict.
paper.abstract: To survive, animals must balance opportunity and risk, yet how internal motivational state biases this trade-off remains poorly understood. Here, we show that hunger gates avoidance of a noxious stimulus in Drosophila to enable food approach under conflict. Using a behavioral assay in which flies must cross an electric shock barrier to reach food, we find that starvation promotes shock tolerance only when food-related olfactory cues are present. This state- and context-dependent behavioral shift is mediated by a defined neuromodulatory circuit. Leucokinin neurons encode hunger and convey this information to PV5K1 lateral horn output neurons, which integrate internal state signals with food odor cues and suppress shock-responsive FB2B neurons in the ventral fan-shaped body. Accordingly, electric shock-evoked activity in FB2B neurons is suppressed in starved flies exposed to food cues. These findings identify a circuit mechanism by which motivational state gates aversive processing to bias action selection towards goal-directed behavior.

Internal validation and resampling stability supported two groups with higher or lower overall bitterness ratings. Five exploratory subgroups described stimulus-specific patterns within these groups. In the full sensory cohort, PROP status alone did not capture the full range of bitterness-response patterns. The five subgroups remain exploratory and require independent replication.

paper.title: Deciphering the key drivers of enhanced floral aroma and reduced bitterness in jasmine tea during multi-round scenting through integrated multi-omics, electronic sensory, and molecular docking analyses.

paper.title: Altered flavor perception among GLP-1 receptor agonist users and product development strategies in the food industry - A review.

Overall, this review provides timely insights into flavor perception changes and food product development strategies to better meet the sensory and nutritional needs of the expanding GLP-1 RA users.

paper.title: A proposed cholinergic phenotype of Parkinson's disease: candidate clinical, biofluid, and imaging markers.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Various non-motor symptom (NMS)-dominant clinical subtypes are recognised in Parkinson's disease (PD), and a cognitive dysfunction-dominant "cholinergic subtype" has also been proposed. In a subset of patients with PD, a cognitive dysfunction-dominant phenotype identified using clinical tests can be recognised and has been termed the "cholinergic" subtype. In this narrative review of the proposed cholinergic subtype, we provide details of clinical, biofluid, and imaging markers that may help further define and refine this non-motor subtype of PD, although the majority of biomarkers remain exploratory.

METHODS: We reviewed the available English-language literature published between 2000 and 2025 that was identified through Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science.

RESULTS: Based on the cross-sectional and longitudinal data from the Cambridgeshire Parkinson's Incidence from GP to Neurologist (CamPaIGN) study, we identified two clinical tests-copying an intersecting pentagon and assessing semantic fluency-as the clinical anchors and constructed a clinical phenotype of late-onset PD characterised by hyposmia, constipation, low body weight, high frailty, gait dysfunction, and other cognitive and neuropsychiatric deficits as associated features. Potential biomarkers, such as plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) and imaging of the nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM), remain exploratory and need to be studied in well-enriched and well-characterised cholinergic PD cohorts.

CONCLUSION: This narrative review describes a proposed clinical phenotype of the cholinergic subtype of PD, which needs to be validated, and highlights that the majority of biomarkers remain exploratory.

paper.title: The K+-dependent Na+/Ca2+-exchanger 4 is localized to intracellular membranes and modulates Ca2+ signaling and proteostasis in choroid plexus epithelial cells.

The NCKX4 protein expressed in CPECs contains an additional 19 amino acids due to alternative splicing, and immunolabeling indicated that it localizes to small acidic compartments likely associated with secretory and/or endosomal pathways. Loss of NCKX4 did not lead to detectable changes in CPEC ultrastructure or ventricular volume. However, proteomic screening of choroid plexus tissues from wildtype and Nckx4-/- mice showed alterations in protein abundance and expression profiles, while cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteomic profiles and ionic concentrations remained unchanged. CPECs lacking NCKX4 displayed similar Ca2+ signal dynamics to wildtype controls under baseline conditions, but showed a slower decay of the Ca2+ signal following strong serotonin stimulation. Together, these data highlight the intracellular localization of NCKX4, its contribution to Ca2+ handling in CPECs, and its novel role in protein homeostasis in the choroid plexus.

paper.title: Schizophrenia heterogeneity, treatment response to clozapine, and the Johns Hopkins Schizoaffective Disorders Precision Medicine Center of Excellence.
paper.abstract: Schizophrenia heterogeneity has resisted resolution for over a century, with no unifying clinical feature, biomarker, or pathogenic pathway identified. This has produced imprecise diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment, while confounding mechanistic research. Prior subtyping approaches-based on clinical phenotype, longitudinal course, age of onset, neuroimaging, physiological measures, or etiological factors-have yielded partial insights but lack established clinical utility. The Johns Hopkins Schizoaffective Disorder Precision Medicine Center of Excellence (PMCOE) brings together patients and clinicians at the Johns Hopkins Hospital and the Johns Hopkins Bayview Community Psychiatry Program with Johns Hopkins schizophrenia investigators to address this heterogeneity through stratification by treatment response, dividing patients into non-treatment-resistant (nonTRS), clozapine-responsive treatment-resistant (crTRS), and ultra-treatment-resistant (uTRS) subgroups. The term "Schizoaffective Disorder" was chosen to include schizophrenia with varying degrees of affective symptomatology, deliberately creating a broadly inclusive patient group. We hypothesize that these subtypes reflect distinct pathophysiological processes and that identifying their biological correlates will improve clinical decision-making and reveal novel therapeutic targets. The PMCOE pursues this hypothesis across four aims. Aim 1 characterizes clinical, cognitive, functional, quality-of-life, and olfactory signatures distinguishing subtypes, with preliminary data showing worse cognition and function in uTRS versus crTRS, and a temporal sequence of clozapine benefit (symptoms, then function, then quality of life). Aim 2 applies 7T structural/functional MRI-including novel measures of microvascular perfusion (iVASO) and CSF clearance (cDSC)-alongside EEG-based dynamic causal and network modeling to probe excitatory/inhibitory imbalance across subtypes. Aim 3 investigates cellular and molecular mechanisms, particularly protein homeostasis dysfunction, using patient-derived induced neurons, organoids, and extracellular vesicles, with focused study of SCHEMA-identified risk genes, including CUL1. Aim 4 leverages electronic health record data to generate validated electronic phenotypes for treatment-response subtypes and to establish a learning health system translating findings into clinical practice. By anchoring subtyping to an empirically measurable, clinically actionable outcome, the PMCOE aims to accelerate biomarker discovery for clozapine response, clarify mechanisms of treatment resistance, and transform care for individuals with schizophrenia-particularly those with ultra-treatment-resistant illness, for whom therapeutic options remain critically limited.

paper.title: Clock misalignment, not structural loss, underlies memory impairment following disruption of the mushroom body.

These findings indicate that memory impairments after HU treatment can arise from disrupted temporal coordination within the MB circuit and demonstrate that downstream MBON-DAN interactions can support learning when properly regulated.

paper.title: Macrophage Gα Chaperone Protein Ric-8B Exacerbates Atherosclerosis.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Macrophage stimulatory G-protein (Gαs/olf)-cAMP signaling promotes cholesterol accumulation and inflammasome activation in atherosclerosis. How obesity-associated inflammation amplifies this pathway is unknown.

METHODS: We studied human and murine macrophages, genetically modified low-density lipoprotein receptor-deficient (Ldlr-/-) bone marrow chimeras, and human carotid plaques using biochemical assays and a macrophage-targeted resistance to inhibitors of cholinesterase 8B (Ric-8B)-Gα interference peptide.

RESULTS: oxLDL (oxidized low-density lipoprotein) activated Gαolf through OR6A2 (olfactory receptor 6A2) and Gαs through downregulation of phosphorylated Gα-interacting vesicle-associated protein (p-GIV [phosphorylated Gα-interacting vesicle-associated protein]); both required Ric-8B. Ric-8B bound nucleotide-free Gαolf and Gαs with high affinity (KD, 21 and 29 nmol/L) through Arg75 and promoted their folding, stability, membrane localization, and cAMP signaling. Disrupting this interface reduced macrophage inflammasome activation and cholesterol accumulation. In Ldlr-/- chimeras, the targeted interference peptide localized to plaque macrophages, suppressed lesional Gαs/olf activity, and reduced atherosclerosis; these effects were absent with a nonbinding control peptide or Ric-8BR75E. In male patients' carotid plaques, plasma IFN-γ (interferon-γ) correlated with macrophage-associated Ric-8B S468/T473 phosphorylation. IFN-γ activated a STAT1 (signal transducer and activator of transcription 1)-independent ERK2 (extracellular signal-regulated kinase 2)-casein kinase 2 α catalytic subunit pathway that phosphorylated Ric-8B at S468/T473, enhancing chaperone activity. Phosphomimetic substitution lowered the pooled fitted oxLDL EC50 for cAMP generation (11.5 versus 27.7 µg/mL in wild-type cells) without increasing basal cAMP; replicate-level EC50 estimates did not differ significantly (P=0.17). This substitution restored the atherogenic phenotype suppressed by Ifngr1 deficiency in obese, but not nonobese, chimeras.

CONCLUSIONS: Ric-8B sustains macrophage Gαs/olf-cAMP signaling and atherogenesis. Obesity-associated IFN-γ enhances macrophage responses to oxLDL through STAT1-independent ERK2-casein kinase 2 α catalytic subunit-Ric-8B signaling, supporting a 2-hit mechanism and identifying the Ric-8B-Gα interface as a potential therapeutic target.

paper.title: Natural predator-associated chemosignals evoke distinct spatiotemporal patterns of risk assessment and vomeronasal population responses.
paper.abstract: Natural predator-associated chemosignals elicit diverse defensive behaviors, yet it remains unclear how complex natural cues shape the spatiotemporal organization of risk assessment and activate vomeronasal sensory neurons (VSNs) and downstream circuits in the mammalian accessory olfactory system. We developed a pose-based integrative machine-learning analysis pipeline (PIMAP) to identify behavioral signatures based on posture, spatial exploration, state transitions, and temporal dynamics. We found that common behavioral states were expressed in multiple odor conditions, but their expression rates, spatial positions, and temporal sequencing distinguished responses to snake, tortoise, lizard, and mouse fecal cues. Snake fecal cues elicited sustained direct investigation and distinct patterns of spatial exploration, behavioral transitions, and grooming in both two-chamber and multiple-choice assays. Volumetric calcium imaging in the vomeronasal epithelium revealed distinct patterns of VSN activation by different reptilian cues. Whole-brain microscopy of FosTRAP2 transgenic mice indicated potential differential activity patterns in AOS-associated circuits following snake and tortoise exposure. Furthermore, Trpc2 deletion altered snake-associated behavioral signatures, while odor-discriminative behavioral patterns remained detectable. Together, these findings show that reptilian predator cues activate distinct AOS components and bias exploration patterns towards threat assessment and vigilance.

paper.title: Effect of Posterior Nasal Nerve Ablation on Biomarker Expression in Patients With Chronic Rhinitis.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated changes in inflammatory and neurogenic biomarkers in nasal secretions in relation to clinical outcomes following temperature-controlled radiofrequency (TCRF) posterior nasal nerve (PNN) ablation in patients with allergic (AR) and nonallergic (NAR) chronic rhinitis (CR).

METHODS: In this prospective multicenter study, 25 participants with moderate to severe CR underwent TCRF PNN ablation. Nasal secretions were collected at baseline and 3 months postprocedure and analyzed for inflammatory biomarkers (ECP, EGF, IFNγ, IgE, IL-1β, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-13, IL-17A, IL-17F, IL-22, IL-25, TNFα) and TRPV1, a sensory nerve marker. Reflective total nasal symptom scores (rTNSS) were assessed from baseline through 6 months.

RESULTS: Mean rTNSS decreased from 7.8 (95% CI: 7.0 to 8.7) at baseline to 4.3 (95% CI: 3.2 to 5.4) at 3 months, a 46% improvement; 75% of participants met responder criteria. Reductions were observed in TRPV1 (0.76-fold) and in epithelial derived IL-25 (0.89-fold) across AR and NAR patients. Reductions in IL-8 were associated with greater treatment response.

CONCLUSIONS: TCRF PNN ablation was associated with symptom improvement in both AR and NAR patients with reduction in neurogenic and epithelial biomarkers, including TRPV1 and IL-25. These findings provide preliminary evidence that TCRF PNN ablation may be a neuroimmune modulatory therapy for CR.
