paper.title: Regenerative epithelial spike cells instruct immune niche homeostasis in zebrafish fin epidermis.
paper.abstract: Epithelia comprise diverse specialized epithelial cells that interact with immune cells, yet how these interactions sustain immune cell pools remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis with transgenic assays in zebrafish and discovered a previously unrecognized epithelial population marked by advillin ( avil) . We identified epithelial cells exhibiting unique morphology and localization, characterized by an apical spike projecting outward from the body - which we term spike cells. These cells exhibit features reminiscent of mammalian tuft cells. Notably, avil + spike cells exhibit close spatial association with a subset of mpeg1 + immune cells. Following fin amputation, spike cells are replenished de novo from precursors and undergo dynamic changes in density, morphology, and orientation, and their regeneration depends on Alk signaling. Moreover, spike cells dynamically interact with mpeg1 + immune cells to maintain the immune cell population. Together, our findings identify a unique epithelial population in zebrafish fins and define their roles in maintaining immune cell niche dynamics.

paper.title: Perceived Bitterness of Antidesma bunius Berries Is Inversely Related to hTAS2R38-PAV Diplotype.
paper.abstract: Sensitivity to bitterness from Antidesma bunius fruit was previously reported to be inversely correlated with the ability to taste bitterness from phenylthiocarbamide (PTC). paper.title: X-ray based 3D histology provides new anatomical and clinical insights into the human cribriform plate region.
paper.abstract: Detailed knowledge of the cribriform plate (CP) microanatomy, a fragile nasal-cranial interface, is important for studying olfaction, preventing iatrogenic injury, and managing cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leaks. Here, we used cryogenic contrast-enhanced microCT (cryo-CECT), a nondestructive X-ray-based 3D histology approach, to image two cadaveric CP-region specimens. We reconstructed a subset of olfactory fila from the lamina propria across the CP toward the olfactory bulbs and delineated the anterior ethmoidal artery and nerve, including vascular branches traversing olfactory foramina. Finally, color-coded thickness maps revealed regional heterogeneity in these specimens, suggesting that micrometer-scale mapping may refine assumptions about structurally vulnerable areas and support larger-scale anatomical and surgical-risk studies.

paper.title: Navigating the Nasal-Brain Nexus: Intranasal Delivery of Therapeutics for Brain Tumors - from Direct Nose-to-Brain Transport to Multidimensional Antitumor Mechanisms.
paper.abstract: Intranasal drug delivery represents a non-invasive, brain-targeted therapeutic strategy that bypasses the blood-brain barrier primarily through the olfactory and trigeminal nerve pathways, enabling efficient therapeutic entry into the central nervous system for brain tumor treatment. This review systematically examines the anatomical foundations, pharmacokinetic profiles, and therapeutic applications of this route in glioblastoma (GB), medulloblastoma, and meningioma. Based on nasal mucosal physiology, delivery systems are classified into solutions, gels, particulate carriers, and nanovesicles. Their design must match mucus thickness, mucociliary clearance, and target expression to achieve prolonged retention and precise delivery. Material selection-including natural/synthetic polymers, lipids, and biomimetic membranes-offers distinct advantages; physicochemical parameters such as size, surface charge, and deacetylation degree critically influence mucus penetration, cellular uptake, and biocompatibility. Intranasal delivery significantly increases brain drug concentration and tumor targeting index, prolonging survival in animal models. It exerts multidimensional antitumor effects by modulating neurotransmitters, reshaping neuroinflammation, regulating neuronal plasticity and circuits, influencing the gut-microbiota-brain axis, and intervening in epigenetic mechanisms. Preliminary clinical trials confirm safety and potential efficacy, but challenges remain: dose limitations, inter-individual variability, formulation stability, and unclear regulatory pathways. Future research should focus on smart responsive systems, nasal-brain tumor pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic models, and patient-specific 3D-printed nasal models to enhance diagnostic-therapeutic integration. Combining in situ imaging, cross-species physiological databases, and standardized guidelines may accelerate clinical translation, positioning intranasal delivery as a key component of comprehensive brain tumor therapy.

paper.title: Bypassing the Blood-Brain Barrier: A Dual-Axis Framework for Parkinson's Disease Utilizing Glymphatic-Lymphatic Clearance and In Situ Chaperone Synthesis.
paper.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized neuropathologically by loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta and by aggregation of misfolded alpha-synuclein into Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites, which is proposed to propagate in a prion-like manner following a stereotyped, stage-dependent pattern described by Braak staging. Because any circulating agent intended to act within the central nervous system (CNS) must cross the blood-brain barrier, this review proposes active craniospinal tensioning (ACT), a mechanical, non-pharmacological route to disease modification acting on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and cerebral venous pressure dynamics. ACT combines two concurrent mechanisms converging on a single venous-side target within Monro-Kellie/Queckenstedt pressure continuity: suboccipital venous occlusion-rebound, proposed to raise and release craniospinal CSF pressure to accelerate venous-side glymphatic efflux, and dural pull-recoil, a reverse Queckenstedt effect in which spinal elongation is proposed to generate a CSF-side pressure gradient with a coupled venous component. The proposed disease-modifying route is clearance of transiting extracellular alpha-synuclein from the perivascular and interstitial space before it templates a neighboring cell. The claim is scoped to the CNS phase of PD, excluding peripheral vagal or olfactory transport, with its most direct anatomical rationale at the dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus (DMV), one of the two earliest CNS sites of Lewy pathology in Braak staging and adjacent to ACT's craniocervical site of action, where ACT is proposed to act on onward extracellular spread rather than on arrival. A secondary, hypothesis-generating axis, cerebral venous preconditioning (CVPC), proposes that the same cycle produces venule- and capillary-wall strain sufficient to activate heat shock factor 1 (HSF-1) within the neurovascular unit, beginning at the vessel wall, independent of oxygen tension, with a possible contribution from hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α) left open; the mechanical route alone is proposed as sufficient. Validation is staged, with diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) and neuromelanin-sensitive magnetic resonance imaging with quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) of the substantia nigra as dual falsification endpoints over at least two years, and any disease-modification claim deferred to a randomized, delayed-start trial. This framework is entirely theoretical, requires clinical validation, and extends a dual-axis template already applied to Alzheimer's disease (AD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

paper.title: First molecular evidence of neglected Lophomonas infection among patients with chronic sinusitis undergoing functional endoscopic sinus sampling: a registry based-study.
paper.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Lophomonas spp. are emerging protozoan pathogens documented in lower respiratory tract infections, yet their potential involvement in upper respiratory conditions, particularly chronic sinusitis, remains entirely unexplored. Unfavorably, chronic sinusitis often proves refractory to standard antibacterial and antifungal therapies, a treatment-failure pattern that raises the possibility of overlooked protozoal etiologies. To date, no registry-based studies have investigated Lophomonas in sinus specimens, and the parasite is not considered in the differential diagnosis of chronic sinusitis. This study aimed to address this knowledge gap by investigating the presence of Lophomonas infection through both microscopic and molecular methods in patients with chronic sinusitis refractory to conventional therapy in northern Iran.

RESULTS: Sinus lavage fluid (SLF) specimens were collected from 30 patients with clinically and radiologically confirmed chronic sinusitis at two teaching hospitals. Samples were analyzed using direct light microscopy and an in-house conventional PCR assay targeting the genus-specific small subunit ribosomal RNA gene (SSU rRNA). Lophomonas was detected in 14 out of 30 patients (46.6%; 95% CI: 30.2%-63.9%). Perfect diagnostic concordance (100%) was observed between microscopy and PCR. No statistically significant associations were found between infection status and demographic variables or recorded comorbidities. The most common clinical presentations included headache, nasal congestion, hyposmia, rhinorrhea, and post-nasal drip (PND), with pansinusitis being the predominant computed tomography finding.

paper.title: Repeated enrichment of hexyl acetate in coreid bugs sympatric with weaver ants.
paper.abstract: Predator-prey interactions are important potential drivers of chemical defense evolution, but how specific predators shape defensive composition remains unclear. Weaver ants (Oecophylla smaragdina) exert strong predation pressure on arboreal insects, offering a model to test links between sympatry and chemical defense variation. Integrating distribution, chemical, and phylogenetic data for 45 coreid bug species, we show that coreids share a conserved chemical repertoire (aldehydes, alcohols, acids, esters), with no overall difference in major compound classes between sympatric and allopatric species. However, sympatric lineages exhibit a significantly higher occurrence frequency of hexyl acetate, with its occurrence distributed across multiple phylogenetic lineages. Bioassays revealed that the four tested esters showed measurable contact toxicity and repellency against O. smaragdina workers, whereas the tested aldehydes and alcohols showed weaker or contrasting effects, with hexyl acetate being particularly notable for its behavioral potency. In contrast, acetic acid and hexanol exhibited marked attractiveness to the ants. This functional reversal highlights the impact of functional group differences on biological activity. Our results are consistent with an association between sympatry and differences in the occurrence of specific compounds within a shared chemical repertoire, rather than gain or loss of compound classes. The association of hexyl acetate with sympatric lineages, together with its strong olfactory and behavioral effects on weaver ants, identifies it as a candidate compound for predator-associated chemical defense. However, whether predator-mediated selection contributed to its repeated occurrence remains unresolved.

paper.title: SlitOBP9 contributes to cis-3-hexenol recognition and larval orientation in Spodoptera litura.

These findings may provide a basic mechanistic lead for future studies, but further work is needed before any practical pest-control application can be considered.

paper.title: Reproducible transversal mouse brain sections using low-cost 3D printable resin matrix.
paper.abstract: Rodent brain matrices that produce coronal or sagittal brain sections for histology confer reproducibility and enable high throughput processing of tissues. The information presented here should assist researchers in focusing future studies on the most relevant appetite-related outcomes.

paper.title: OLFM4 exacerbates neutrophilic asthma progression by modulating the interaction between neutrophils and airway epithelial cells.
paper.abstract: Neutrophilic asthma (NA) represents a distinct asthma subtype that responds poorly to standard therapies. Olfactomedin 4 (OLFM4) is a glycoprotein predominantly enriched in neutrophils, the role of which remains unclear in NA. This study aimed to elucidate the functional role and underlying mechanisms of OLFM4 in mediating communication between neutrophils and airway epithelial cells (AECs) in NA. An NA mouse model was established through ovalbumin sensitization combined with cigarette smoke exposure. Disease progression was evaluated by assessing airway hyperresponsiveness, differential leukocyte counts in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), and histopathological alterations. Neutrophil infiltration was detected via immunohistochemical staining for Ly6G and MPO. For in vitro experiments, neutrophil‑like cells differentiated from HL‑60 and BEAS‑2B airway epithelial cells (AECs) were exposed to cigarette smoke extract. Gene and protein expression were examined by qPCR, western blotting, and immunofluorescence, while cell migration was evaluated using Transwell assays. Protein-protein interactions were verified through co‑immunoprecipitation. Analysis of the GSE256534 sequencing dataset revealed that OLFM4 was up-regulated in peripheral blood samples from patients with acute asthma exacerbation. In vivo model demonstrated that OLFM4 was significantly upregulated in neutrophils from NA mice. Overexpression of OLFM4 promoted neutrophil migration, enhanced the secretion of inflammatory cytokines, and activated the MAPK signaling pathway, which were reversed by a MAPK inhibitor. Furthermore, neutrophils were found to transfer OLFM4 to BEAS‑2B cells via exosomes, which subsequently promoted epithelial-mesenchymal transition and extracellular matrix deposition. Mechanistically, OLFM4 bound to BMP7 and impeded its secretion, thereby suppressing smad1/5/8 signaling and modulating AECs function. Finally, knockdown of OLFM4 attenuated NA progression in vivo. Collectively, our findings indicate that OLFM4 exacerbates NA by enhancing neutrophil infiltration and pulmonary fibrosis, offering novel insights into the pathological mechanisms of NA.

paper.title: Divergent Biologic Responses in Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps: Mechanisms of Residual Disease and Longitudinal Management.
paper.abstract: Biologics improve polyp burden, congestion, smell, quality of life, and rescue-treatment outcomes in severe chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP), yet individual responses remain heterogeneous and frequently discordant across clinical domains. This narrative Review examines why trial-level efficacy does not consistently become multidomain disease control. We propose that residual burden arises from five interacting sources: persistent or parallel inflammation, slowly reversible tissue remodeling, anatomy or impaired topical access, olfactory-compartment injury, and implementation failure. Epithelial alarmins, interleukin (IL)-4/IL-13 signaling, immunoglobulin E, eosinophil states, stromal programs, mixed or non-type 2 inflammation, and olfactory epithelial injury overlap rather than define mutually exclusive endotypes. Consequently, blood or tissue biomarkers can support a treatment hypothesis but do not yet predict the superior biologic for an individual patient. Randomized trials establish efficacy for several targets, whereas indirect comparisons, switching cohorts, interval-extension studies, and withdrawal data answer different and less certain questions. We therefore frame biologic treatment as a longitudinal experiment: define the patient-valued target, verify exposure and background care, measure domain-specific trajectories, explain residual disease, and match the next action to the unresolved mechanism. Emotional distress, adherence, affordability, and access are integrated within implementation failure because they determine whether pharmacological efficacy becomes durable real-world control. Future studies should prioritize treatment-interaction biomarkers, tissue-informed response phenotypes, direct comparisons, adaptive sequencing trials, and explicit definitions of on-treatment and treatment-free remission.

paper.title: Allergen Sensitization and Cytokine Signatures in Allergic Rhinitis in Ningxia, China.
paper.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Regional allergen profiles and local mucosal inflammation may contribute to heterogeneity in allergic rhinitis (AR). We characterized allergen sensitization patterns in Ningxia and explored associations between nasal inflammatory mediators and clinical burden.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 2726 consecutive outpatients evaluated for AR who underwent serum allergen-specific IgE testing from January 2023 to January 2026, together with a prospective exploratory substudy of 47 participants who underwent clinical assessment, nasal lavage, and measurement of 15 inflammatory mediators. Associations with Total Nasal Symptom Score (TNSS), Questionnaire of Olfactory Disorders-Negative Statements (QOD-NS), and Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) were examined using partial least squares regression with repeated cross-validation and 5,000 bootstrap resamples.

RESULTS: Sensitization to at least one allergen was detected in 1,471/2,726 patients (53.96%). Mugwort was the most frequently positive allergen (797/2,726, 29.24%), and pollen allergens predominated among sensitized patients, with monthly test positivity increasing markedly in late summer and early autumn. In the exploratory substudy, higher nasal IFN-γ and IL-1β were bootstrap-stable correlates of higher TNSS. Higher IFN-γ, IL-1β, and IL-6 and lower IL-10 were stably associated with worse olfaction-related quality of life. No cytokine met the predefined stability criteria for HAMD.

CONCLUSION: Mugwort-dominant pollen sensitization and pronounced temporal variation in test positivity characterize this clinical population in Ningxia. Exploratory nasal cytokine analyses suggest that IFN-γ-, IL-1β-, IL-6-, and IL-10-related mucosal activity may accompany symptom and olfaction-related burden. These associations are hypothesis-generating, do not establish causality or inflammatory endotypes, and require validation in larger prospective cross-sectional analysis.

paper.title: Six Years after the Storm: Drawing the First Line on COVID-19 and Parkinson's Disease.
paper.abstract: Six years after the SARS-CoV-2 outbreak, we revisit the fear of a post-COVID parkinsonism wave, echoing encephalitis lethargica after the 1918 pandemic, through two questions. First, is the infection a risk factor for de novo Parkinson's disease (PD)? Epidemiology reveals no robust signal, yet pathological, imaging, and experimental evidence shows the virus targets the olfactory-brainstem axis, sustains neuroinflammation, promotes α-synuclein aggregation, and leaves a dopaminergic footprint. We hypothesize an inflammation-driven, rather than directly cytopathic, mechanism in vulnerable individuals, with persistent post-COVID hyposmia as a candidate risk marker. As the PD prodrome outlasts available follow-up, this question remains open. Second, does infection alter the trajectory of established PD? Motor and non-motor worsening during and shortly after COVID-19 is consistently demonstrated. However, accelerated neurodegeneration remains unproven. Neither alarm nor reassurance is warranted, but long-term, prospective, harmonized cohorts enriched for hyposmia and characterized with α-synuclein seed amplification assays, neurofilament light chain, and dopamine transporter imaging are needed. © 2026 International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

paper.title: An active inference theory of wine tasting and expertise.
paper.abstract: Wine tasting is a complex, naturalistic behavior that recruits a diverse array of sensory, motor, cognitive, affective, and social processes. Yet research on wine tasting has lacked a formal framework that can unify these processes, organize existing findings, and generate precise predictions to guide future work. To address this need, we propose a formal, computational account of wine tasting and wine expertise grounded in active inference. In this framework, wine tasting can be understood as a dynamic cycle of perceptual inference, policy selection, and action. We begin by introducing active inference in the context of wine tasting and then review behavioral, computational, and neuroscientific work that is broadly consistent with this perspective. We further develop an account of wine expertise by mapping the core components of active inference onto the perceptual, cognitive, and learning processes through which expertise is acquired and refined over time. Finally, we highlight future directions for wine research, including formal model comparison, real-time measurement of tasting behavior, and developmental approaches to expertise.

paper.title: Investigation of the key aroma-active compounds in Fangxian Huangjiu using sensory-directed flavor omics.
paper.abstract: Huangjiu is one of the world's three major fermented alcoholic drinks. Three Fangxian Huangjiu (FXHJ) samples: Fuzhi-style (13.7% vol, pH 4.32), refreshing-style (10.3% vol, pH 3.64), and traditional-style (17.3% vol, pH 4.14), were analyzed. The key aroma-active compounds were characterized using a sensory-directed flavor omics approach. A total of 83 odorants were identified in the study using solvent-assisted flavor evaporation (SAFE) combined with gas chromatography-olfactometry-mass spectrometry (GC-O-MS), along with odor specific magnitude estimation (Osme) and aroma extract dilution analysis (AEDA). Among them, 11 were newly identified as odorants in FXHJ. After quantitation, there were 29 compounds with odor activity values (OAVs) ≥ 1. Similarities of aroma profiles between the three FXHJ recombinant models and their corresponding original samples were higher than 95%. Finally, 2-methyl-1-butanol, 4-hydroxyphenylethanol, linalool, (E)-β-ionone, α-ionone, 2-methylpropionic acid, γ-decalactone, and ethyl 3-hydroxybutanoate were first confirmed as key aroma-active compounds of FXHJ using omission tests.

paper.title: Sensorimotor impairment and cognitive function across the Alzheimer's disease continuum and major depressive disorder.
paper.abstract: Sensorimotor impairments are associated with cognitive decline, but their cumulative burden across clinical subgroups is not well characterized. To test whether sensorimotor burden is associated with baseline cognition and modifies subgroup-related cognitive differences. We analyzed 511 community-dwelling older adults. Participants were classified as cognitively normal, preclinical Alzheimer's disease (Clinical Dementia Rating score of 0 with amyloid positron-emission tomography positivity), mild cognitive impairment, or major depressive disorder. Cognition was measured with the Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite. A Sensorimotor Index summed impairments in grip strength, gait speed, reaction time, hearing, vision, and olfaction and was categorized as low (0-1) or elevated (≥ 2). Multivariable linear regression assessed subgroup, index, and subgroup-by-index terms, adjusting for age, sex, race, education, apolipoprotein E ε4 status, and neighborhood deprivation. Without interactions, elevated burden was associated with lower cognitive scores (β =- 0.374; 95% confidence interval, - 0.508 to - 0.240; p < 0.001). In the interaction model, the mild cognitive impairment-by-elevated-index (β =- 0.647; 95% confidence interval, - 0.981 to - 0.313; p < 0.001) and major depressive disorder-by-elevated-index terms (β =- 0.440; 95% confidence interval, - 0.759 to - 0.120; p = 0.007) were significant; the preclinical Alzheimer's disease interaction was not. Dose-response analyses showed progressively lower cognitive scores at higher index levels. Greater sensorimotor burden was associated with lower cognition, with stronger adverse associations in mild cognitive impairment and major depressive disorder. Multidomain sensorimotor assessment may improve characterization of cognitive heterogeneity in older adults.

paper.title: [A new chemical biology strategy for studying four natures and five flavors theory of traditional Chinese medicine].
paper.abstract: The four natures and five flavors theory is one of the core frameworks in traditional Chinese medicine(TCM) for characterizing the medicinal properties and action patterns of Chinese materia medica. However, its modern interpretation remains limited by the gap between empirical description and mechanism understanding. From the perspective of TCM chemical biology, this review takes the Four Natures and Five Flavors theory as a starting point and proposes an experimentally testable research strategy. We suggest that the medicinal properties associated with the Four Natures and Five Flavors may arise from the coordinated actions of multiple natural constituents on chemosensory targets and related functional networks. Current evidence indicates that natural products can act on G protein-coupled receptors, transient receptor potential channels, and other chemosensory proteins, thereby modulating target conformations and downstream signaling and providing molecular entry points for investigating nature-and flavor-related properties. Advances in structural biology now enable the recognition modes and conformational changes of natural molecules interacting with their target proteins to be resolved at near-atomic detail, while AI-assisted structure prediction and molecular simulation provide complementary tools for mechanistic analysis and candidate screening. On this basis, we propose a TCM chemical biology framework in which pharmacologically active constituents serve as the material basis and nature-and flavor-related targets as mechanistic entry points, with particular emphasis on target conformational regulation, cellular and molecular mechanisms, and validation of disease-and syndrome-related phenotypes. This framework may provide a basis for modern studies of the Four Natures and Five Flavors theory and support TCM quality evaluation, bioactive constituent discovery, and innovative drug research.

paper.title: Scent Marking Mediates Spatial Interactions between Two Sympatric Mesocarnivores in Central Mongolia.
paper.abstract: Scent marking is a fundamental component of carnivore communication and can mediate spatial interactions among sympatric species. In this study, we investigated olfactory marking behaviour and interspecific interactions between Pallas's cat (Otocolobus manul) and red fox (Vulpes vulpes) in the central Mongolian steppe. We aimed to assess whether Pallas's cat exhibits spatial or temporal responses to red fox scent marks. We analyzed data from a continuous camera-trapping survey conducted between August 2020 and August 2024 across 57 sites, totaling 32,722 trap-days. Independent detection events involving olfactory behaviors were classified into scent-producing and scent-investigative categories. Spatial associations of the marking sites for both species were evaluated using contingency analyses, while temporal responses were assessed by comparing the time intervals between successive marking events. Pallas's cat and red fox were recorded in 267 and 798 independent detection events, respectively, with marking activity detected at 45 of the 57 camera-trap sites. Pallas's cat exhibited six types of olfactory behaviors, whereas red fox exhibited five, with olfactory investigation being the most frequent behavior in both species. Spatial analyses revealed a strong negative association between Pallas's cat and red fox marking sites, indicating marked spatial segregation consistent with avoidance by Pallas's cat. In contrast, no significant difference was detected in the temporal intervals between Pallas's cat markings following red fox activity and intervals between consecutive conspecific markings. These findings demonstrate that Pallas's cat responds to red fox presence primarily through spatial avoidance rather than temporal adjustment of marking behavior. This pattern suggests asymmetric interspecific interactions, potentially reflecting avoidance by Pallas's cat in response to red fox presence, highlighting the role of spatial mechanisms in structuring carnivore coexistence in open steppe ecosystems.
